NAGRAMPA Punong Barangay San Vicente Sur, City of Iriga Dear Punong Barangay Nagrampa, This pertains to your letter dated February 5, 20171, seeking verification on the legality of an Order dated February I, 2017, issued by Mayor Madelaine Yorobe Alfelor, City Ofo Iriga. For clarity, the said order is hereby quoted in toto: "Pursuant to the Decision dated January 9, 2017 of the Office of the Sangguniang Panhtngsod in the case entitled GENEROSO A. ALBINO, et.al., Complainants, versus PB BENGIE R. NAGRAMPA, Respondent, docketed as Administrative Case NO. 2016-03, the Undersigned issued an Order Of Suspension dated rebruary l, 2017, the dispositive portion reads, thus: "WHEREFORE, Punong Barangay BENJIE R. NAGRAMPA is hereby suspended for a period of six (6) months effective immediately and is ordered to vacate his office as the Punong Barangay of San Vicente Sur, Iriga City. SO ORDERED. In connection with the earlier Order, and in accordance with the pertinent provision of Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991, Barangay Kagawad DIONISIO D. NACARIO, being the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member: of San Vicente Sur, Iriga City, is ordered to fill up the 1 Addressed to Atty. Cinderella F. vacancy and exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Punong Barangay of San Vicente Sur, Iriga City. SO ORDERED. February 1, 2017, Irig City, Philippines. sgd. MADELAINE YOROBE ALFELOR City Mayor" According to you, Kagawad Dionisio D. Nacario is a former Punong Barangay who had alre dy completed three terms in office, his last term having ended in 2013. Upon completion of his term, Punong Barangay Nacario ran in the last barangay elections and won as the first ranking Barangay Kagawad. Hence, it is now your contention that Kagawad Nacario, having previously completed his three terms as Punong Barangay is now disqualified from assuming the office of the Punong Barangay in view of your suspension for the period of six (6) 'months. Your contention is anchored on Section 43 (b) of Republic Act No. +160 or the Local Government Code of 19912 as well as Section 8, Article X oft the 1987 Philippine Constitution3. In reply to your request, may we first invite your attention to Section 46 of Republic Act No. 7 60 which explicitly provides: "SEC. 46. Term of Office. - (a) Thet rm of office of all local elective officials elected after the effectivity of this Code shall be three (3) years, starting from noon of June 30, 1992 or such date as may be provided for by law, except that of elective Barangay officials: Prov ded, That all local officials first elected during the local elections immediately following the ratification of the 198 Constitution shall serve until noon Of June 30, 1992. (b) NO local elective official shall serve for more than three (3) onsecutive terms in the same position. Voluntary renunciation of the office for any length of time shall not be as an interruption in the continuity of service for the full term for which the elective official concerned wus elected. (c) The term of office of Barangay officials and members of the Sangguniang Kabataan shall be for three (3) years, which shall begin after the regular election of Barangay officials on the second Monday of May 1994." 3 "Section 8. The term of office of elective local officials, except barangay officials, which shall be determined by law, shall be three years and no such official shall serve for more than three consecutive terms. Voluntary renunciation Of the office for any length of time Shall not be considered as an interruption in the continuity of his service for the full term for which he was elected. 2

(b) Said temporary incapacity shall terminate upon submission to the appropriate Sanggunian of a written declaration by the local chief executive concerned that he has reported back to office. In cases where the temporary incapacity is due to legal causes, the local chief executive concerned shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal cause no longer exist. (c) When the incumbent local chief executive is traveling within the country but outside his territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days, he may designate in writing the officer-in-charge of the said office. Such authorization shall specify the powers and functions that the local official concerned shall exercise in the absence Of the local chief executive except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees. (d) In the event, however, that the local chief executive concerned fails or refuses to issue uch authorization, the vice-governor, the city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay member, as the case may be, shall have the right to assume the powers, duties, and functions of the said office on the fourth (4th) day of absence of the said local chief executive, subject to the limitations provided in subsection (c) hereof. (e) Except as provided above, the logal chief execg$ive shall in no case wers utie an authorize any local ffici o assum functions ot the office, other than the vice gqverner, the city or municipal vice- Mayor the hi hest r kin San unian B an a rnembec, as the case may be. (Emphasis supplied) Verily, based on he foregoing provisions of law, when the Punong Barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, b t not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from omce, the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Punong Barangay, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees whic can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirt (30) working days. Thus, applying the law in the instant query, in view of your suspension from office for a period of six months pursuant to the decision of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Iriga, Barangay Kagawad Dionisio D. Nacario, as the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member of Barangay San Vicente Sur, shall have the right to automatically assume the office of the Punong Barangay. 3

As regards your contention that Kagawad Dionisio D. Nacario is disqualified from assuming the office of the Punong Barangay on the ground that he had already completed three terms in office as Punong Barangay, his last term having ended •n 2013, this Department is of the view that the three- term limit rule does not apply in the present case. It is worth reiterating that Dionisio D. Nacario is a former Punong Barangay who had pr viously completed three terms in office in 2013. Thereafter, he ran in th last barangay elections and won as the first ranking Barangay Kagawad. It is thus quite obvious that during the last barangay elections of 2016, NacÅrio did not run again as Punong Barangay but as Kagawad. His assumption, therefore, as Punong Barangay due to your suspension from office is by virtue of the rule on succession as discussed above and not by electi n to that office. In the landmark ase of Borja vs. COMELEC4 and further bolstered in the case of Lonzanida v . COMELEC5, the Supreme Court has consistently held that in order for the aforementioned three-term limit rule to apply to local elective officials holding the same position, the following requisites must concur: (1) that the official concerned has been elected for three consecutive terms in the same locel government post; and (2) that he has fully served three consecutive terme.6 In view of the fo egoing, this Department so holds the view that there is nothing irregular or iillegal in the aforementioned order issued by Mayor Alfelor ordering Barangay Kagawad Dionisio D. Nacario to fill up the temporary vacancy in the office ot the Punong Barangay and exercise the powers and duties appurtenant thereto, for even without such order, Nacario has to fill up such temporary vacanc automatically as mandated by law. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very t you AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary -O SLG 06-0-0 Enclosure: as stated G.R. No. 133495, September 3, 1 98 G.R.
